AS A RESULT OF THE COVID-19 VIRUS, AND RESULTING ORDERS AND DIRECTION FROM THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES, THE GOVERNOR OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA, AND THE ORANGE COUNTY HEALTH CARE AGENCY, AS WELL AS THE CITY OF IRVINE EMERGENCY DECLARATION, THE PUBLIC WILL NOT BE PERMITTED TO PHYSICALLY ATTEND THE IRVINE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY MEETING TO WHICH THIS AGENDA APPLIES.
MEETINGS ARE BROADCAST LIVE ON ICTV, COX COMMUNICATIONS LOCAL ACCESS CHANNEL 30, AND AT&T U-VERSE CHANNEL 99, AND LIVESTREAMED ONLINE AT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV. YOU MAY ALSO PROVIDE LIVE COMMENTS VIA “ZOOM.” FOR MORE INFORMATION, VISIT CITYOFIRVINE.ORG/ICTV AND SELECT “CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.”
PLEASE NOTE: THE CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY IS MAKING EVERY EFFORT TO FOLLOW THE SPIRIT AND INTENT OF THE BROWN ACT AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF PUBLIC MEETINGS, IN ORDER TO MAXIMIZE TRANSPARENCY AND PUBLIC ACCESS. NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council and Successor Agency meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council and/or Successor Agency meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 10 a.m. until the next City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the City's ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the City Clerk's office at (949) 724-6205.
ADJOURNMENT
At 11:00 p.m., the City Council/Successor Agency will determine which of the remaining agenda items can be considered and acted upon prior to 12:00 midnight and will continue all other items on which additional time is required until a future City Council/Successor Agency meeting. All meetings are scheduled to terminate at 12:00 midnight.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 12 days prior to a regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the City's website at cityofirvine.org at least 12 days prior to the scheduled City Council/Successor Agency meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv .
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Successor Agency regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk's Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Successor Agency Board.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk's Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.

minutes_text:
MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AND
  REGULAR JOINT MEETING
  WITH THE CITY OF IRVINE AS SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY TO THE DISSOLVED IRVINE
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY

  January 26, 2021
  City Council Chamber
  One Civic Center Plaza
  Irvine, CA 92606

CALL TO ORDER
The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council and regular joint meeting with the City of
Irvine as Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency was called to
order at 4:51 p.m. on January 26, 2021, in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center,
One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California; Mayor/Chairwoman Khan presiding.
ROLL CALL
  Present: 5 Councilmember/Boardmember:  Larry Agran*
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Mike Carroll
  Councilmember/Boardmember:  Anthony Kuo
  Vice Mayor/Vice Chairman:  Tammy Kim
  Mayor/Chairwoman  Farrah N. Khan
  *via teleconference

Mayor/Chairwoman Khan announced that the meeting was broadcast live on Cox
Communications Local Access Channel 30 and AT&T U-Verse Channel 99, and
livestreamed online at cityofirvine.org; and that in an effort to protect public health and
prevent the spread of COVID-19, members of the public had the ability to provide live
comments on agenda items using Zoom. She also noted that the e-comment feature had
been extended for all agenda items, which allowed members of the public the ability to
submit e-comments on all agenda items, which would be included as part of the official
record and uploaded to the City’s website. She also assured the community that the City of
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  Irvine was adhering to the Governor’s Executive Order in the Council Chamber and
  throughout City Hall by sanitizing surfaces and equipment, as well as wearing face masks.

  Mayor Khan also announced that general public comments for the City Council on items
  not on the agenda would be considered at approximately 6:30 p.m.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Carroll led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  INVOCATION

  Councilmember Kuo provided the invocation.

  CITY COUNCIL RECOGNITIONS

  ∗  Proclaim January 2021 as “Firefighter Cancer Awareness Month.”

  Mayor Khan expressed her appreciation to the countless firefighters who put their
  health and lives on the line to keep Irvine and other communities safe, and asked
  Councilmember Kuo to read the proclamation as the City’s representative to the
  Orange County Fire Authority, recognizing January, 2021, as “Firefighter Cancer
  Awareness Month.”

  Todd Baldridge, President of the Orange County Professional Fire Fighters, spoke
  in support of the proclamation.

  Jim Farkas inquired about the status of the Veterans Cemetery.

  ∗  Proclaim February 12, 2021, as “Lunar New Year.”

  Mayor Khan presented a proclamation recognizing February 12, 2021 as “Lunar
  New Year,” and expressed her appreciation to Vice Mayor Kim and Councilmember
  Kuo for bringing the item forward.

  Vice Mayor Kim and Councilmember Kuo noted that Lunar New Year was special
  time of the year, and wished everyone a year full of blessings and health.

  1.  PRESENTATIONS

  1.1  Irvine Unified School District

  Dr. Tammy Blakely, Executive Director of Student Support Services, Irvine
  Unified School District (IUSD), presented a brief presentation on IUSD’s
  background, notable accomplishments, health and safety measures
  during the COVID-19 pandemic, and economic status; and expressed
  appreciation to the City Council for its continued support.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  City Council discussion included: expressing appreciation to IUSD for its
  continued partnership with the City of Irvine; expressed concern about the
  ratio of nurses to schools; and suggested that the City consider additional
  resources to allow for one nurse at every Irvine school, including those
  within the Tustin Unified School district that serve Irvine residents.

  Kevin Corrigan, Irvine high school student, expressed concern about
  COVID-19 case rates reflected on IUSD’s website, and suggested that
  IUSD revisit its policy to encourage parents to self-report cases.

  By consensus, received and filed. No action was taken.

  1.2  Assumptions, Baseline Projections and Preliminary Balancing
  Measures for Fiscal Year 2021-23 Two-Year Budget and Fiscal Year
  2021-26 Five-Year Plan

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager; Barbara Arenado, Deputy
  Director of Financial Management & Strategic Planning; Pete Carmichael,
  Director of Community Development; and Joel Belding, Deputy Director
  of Great Park Planning & Development, presented the staff report and
  responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: noting the importance of community
  meetings with respect to the budget process; suggested flexible
  community meeting dates/times to maximize resident participation; noted
  resources available through Public Safety; inquired about the balance in
  the contingency fund and the methodology used to determine its reserve
  level; expressed concern about limiting overtime and implementing a
  hiring freeze, and their potential impacts on service levels; noted the City’s
  historical fiscal management practices; suggested allocating $2 million per
  fiscal year from the contingency reserves to increase the school nurse
  ratio; discussed using funds from the contingency reserve if needed
  during the COVID-19 pandemic to address some of its impacts to the
  community; and inquired about the Bridge Program developed in 2008
  and the population of the City at that time.

  Nissreen, John Youn, and Eugenie, Irvine residents, spoke in opposition
  to the Community Facilities District (CFD) Mello-Roos tax imposed on
  Great Park properties.

  Dee Fox, Irvine resident, spoke in support of Councilmember Agran’s
  suggestion to increase funding for school nurses.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  Jeff Melching, City Attorney, noted that the noted CFD taxes were in
  perpetuity as long as outstanding bonds existed, and removing the CFD
  revenue stream would be in violation of the contract with the bond holders.

  By consensus, received and filed. No action was taken.

  1.3  Capital Improvement Program Update

  Steven Carrillo, Manager of Engineering/City Engineer, provided a brief
  overview of the proposed 5-year Capital Improvement Program, and
  responded to questions. Jaimee Bourgeois, Deputy Director of
  Transportation, also responded to questions.

  Council discussion included: questioning the financial models used to
  project gas tax revenue; suggested the use of indigenous plants for
  landscaping; and questioned whether bike enhancements, including bike
  safety and connectivity, had being considered.

  There were no public comments.

  By consensus, received and filed. No action was taken.

  INTERIM CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Agran noted that he would continue to seek support to agendize his
  proposed resolution for consideration that was brought forward at the last City Council
  meeting to implement provisions of the Build the Great Park Veterans Cemetery Initiative;
  and also noted that he was awaiting a response to his memo requesting a public study
  session be held to address the All American Asphalt issue.

  Mayor Khan noted that she had responded to Councilmember Agran’s memo regarding All
  American Asphalt, and suggested a briefing with staff if he had not yet had the opportunity
  to do so.

  Mayor Khan also clarified that the oversight and enforcement of the industrial emissions
  was the responsibility of Southern California Air Quality Management District (AQMD); and
  that the City has taken measures to evaluate health risk at the plant and protect residents.
  She also noted that the City had requested a public meeting with AQMD and is awaiting a
  response for a specified date.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  Mayor Khan also made the following announcements:

  •  To help answer questions about the COVID-19 vaccine, along with information on
  how and when to get vaccinated, the COVID-19 Task Force will be hosting a Virtual
  Town Hall meeting on Friday, January 29 from noon to 1:30 p.m. The Task Force is
  comprised of members of the City management team, Mayor Khan, and local health
  officials, including:

  •  Dr. Marnie Baker with MemorialCare;
  •  Dr. Clayton Chau, the Orange County Health Officer and Director of
  the Orange County Health Care Agency;
  •  Amy Durham, Director of Development for the National Alliance on
  Mental Illness;
  •  Dr. Shruti Gohil from UC Irvine’s School of Medicine;
  •  Dr. Grace Lozinski from Hoag; and
  •  Dr. Hassan Movahedi from Kaiser Permanente.

  To register for the virtual Town Hall, visit cityofirvine.org. Questions for the COVID-
  19 Task Force can also be submitted when registering for the event.

  •  Applications for the City’s second small business support program are being
  accepted through Friday, January 29. As of January 25, 675 applications had been
  received. One-time grants up to $5,000 are available to help eligible small
  businesses cover the costs of business interruption due to the pandemic and Stay-
  at-Home order. The City received $722,000 from the County of Orange to establish
  the program and assist Irvine small businesses within the Third Supervisorial
  District. Supervisor Donald P. Wagner helped make this program possible.
  Businesses that meet program requirements will be entered into a lottery after the
  application closing date on January 29. Lottery numbers are expected to be posted
  on the City’s web page by 5 p.m. on Wednesday, February 3. To learn more about
  qualifications and to apply, visit cityofirvine.org/ThirdDistrictGrantProgram.

  •  Since the launching of the first initiative of the City’s COVID-19 Task Force, more
  than 530 people have taken the “Irvine Cares” pledge. Irvine Cares invites
  community members to slow the spread of COVID-19 by pledging support of
  mitigation measures, which include acting as an advocate to ensure the health and
  safety of Irvine’s most vulnerable. Community members are invited to take the
  pledge online or download a pledge card and mail it into the City. Once the pledge
  has been signed, names will be included on the “I Pledge” website. Anyone who
  takes the pledge will receive an “Irvine Cares” face mask, sticker, and decal to
  highlight their commitment to being kind and protecting our community. Community
  members are also encouraged to share the pledge on social media using the
  hashtag #IrvineCares. For more information and to take the pledge, visit
  cityofirvine.org/irvinecares.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  •  The City is seeking the community’s feedback to assist in planning the Oak Creek
  Community Park Project. Two online surveys have been launched to gather input
  on potential community park and dog park amenities. The community park survey,
  as well as the survey focused on dog park amenities, are available through January
  31. Input provided will be presented in virtual public meetings held in February and
  will help inform the design of Oak Creek Community Park. For more information and
  to take the surveys, visit cityofirvine.org/oakcreekproject.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  Interim City Manager Marysheva asked that Item No. 2.4 be removed from the Consent
  Calendar for discussion to allow for public participation on the item, and also allow staff to
  amend the proposed lease amount from $48 per month as recommended by staff, to $1
  per year as recommended by the Orange County Great Park Board earlier in the day.

  CONVENE TO THE REGULAR JOINT MEETING

  Mayor/Chairwoman Khan convened to the regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine as
  Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment Agency at 7:13 p.m.

  2.  CONSENT CALENDAR – CITY COUNCIL

  ACTION:  Moved by Councilmember/Boardmember Kuo, seconded by
  Councilmember/Boardmember Carroll, and unanimously carried to approve
  City Council Consent Calendar Item Nos. 2.1 through 2.3, and Successor
  Agency Consent Calendar Item Nos 3.1 and 3.2. City Council Consent
  Calendar Item No. 2.4 was removed for separate discussion.

  2.1  MINUTES

  ACTION:
  1) Approved the minute of a special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on December 8, 2020.
  2) Approved the minutes of a regular meeting of the Irvine City
  Council and regular joint meeting with the City of Irvine as
  Successor Agency to the dissolved Irvine Redevelopment
  Agency held on December 8, 2020.
  3) Approved the minutes of a special meeting of the Irvine City
  Council held on December 21, 2020.

  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING

  ACTION:

  CITY OF IRVINE, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 3-25 OF

  4.1  COVID-19 SITUATIONAL UPDATE AND DIRECTION TO DIRECTOR
  OF EMERGENCY SERVICES ON RELEVANT ACTION ITEMS

  Michelle Grettenberg, Assistant City Manager; Melissa Haley, Deputy City
  Manager; and Pete Carmichael, Director of Community Development,
  presented the staff report responded to questions. Marianna Marysheva,
  Interim City Manager, also provided an update on the progress related to
  the County of Orange selecting a COVID-19 vaccination site; and noted
  that staff continued to work closely with the County of Orange to: 1) open
  a vaccination site no later than February 10; 2) open a separate
  vaccination site for seniors; and 3) provide prioritization for Irvine residents
  at the selected Irvine site.

  City Council discussion included: noting the recent increases in COVID-
  19 cases and deaths in Irvine; expressing concern about the County’s
  rejection of the Orange County Great Park as a mass vaccine distribution
  site; noted correspondence by the Orange County Health Chief Executive
  Officer outlining concerns by FivePoint Communities with respect to
  potential traffic impacts; and reiterated the efforts to work with the Orange
  County Board of Supervisors, the Orange County Health Chief Executive
  Officer, and various other individuals to secure a vaccination distribution
  site.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  9
 City Council Minutes  January 26, 2021

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Agran, seconded by Councilmember
  Kuo, to:

  1) Authorize and direct the Mayor and the Interim City Manager to
  petition the Orange County Board of Supervisors, the Orange
  County Health Agency, and appropriate State and Federal officials,
  expressing the City’s strong determination to establish the City-
  owned Orange County Great Park as a COVID-19 mass
  vaccination site to be operational by February 10, 2021, with
  logistical planning and support provided by the City of Irvine.
  2) Further authorize the Mayor and the Interim City Manager to enlist
  and contract with University of California Irvine/University of
  California Irvine Medical Center and other leading health care
  leading institutions to advise and assist in the organization and
  administration of vaccines, and the provision of nurses and other
  health care professionals, in order to scale the number of COVID-
  19 vaccinations at the Great Park as rapidly as possible with a goal
  administering 500,000 dozes per day by the end of February.

  Continued City Council discussion included: noting that vaccines were
  limited to health care workers and front line workers at this time; reiterated
  the existing vaccine shortage; discussed additional options for mass
  vaccination sites; noted that the decision for site selection would be
  determined by the County; expressed concern that a continued request to
  select the Orange County Great Park as a mass vaccination site may
  delay vaccination distribution; reiterated the need to vaccinate seniors as
  soon as possible; and inquired about what could potentially be
  accomplished by February 10.

  Interim City Manager Marysheva clarified that the County of Orange had
  no control over the supply of vaccines; and that the City and County were
  anticipating the opening of a mass distribution site between February 10
  and February 20.

  Dee Fox, Irvine resident, spoke in support of the motion made by
  Councilmember Agran.

  Empower the City Manager and the County Liaison Committee,
  consisting of Mayor Khan and Councilmember Kuo, to continue
  working collaboratively on the selection of a mass vaccination site
  without delay and without post haste.

  4.2  CITY COUNCIL BUDGET OVERVIEW

  Melissa Haley, Deputy City Manager, and Michelle Greenberg, Assistant
  City Manager, presented the staff report and responded to questions.

  City Council discussion included: discussing Council Executive Assistant
  (CEA) program changes, including budget oversight by the City Manager;
  noted that the proposed policy change would provide each
  Councilmember the opportunity to oversee and manage their own
  individual budgets; questioned the amounts allocated to each
  Councilmember; discussed ensuring oversight measures were in place to
  provide checks and balances; discussed oversight of budgets by
  individual Councilmembers; questioned why the Council Executive
  Assistants (CEAs) were limited to part-time hours; and inquired about the
  approval process for CEA timesheets.

  Marianna Marysheva, Interim City Manager, clarified that staff was
  seeking direction as to whether individualize budgets should be set-up for
  each Councilmember; noted that the existing review process would
  remain intact; and that annual audits would continue to be conducted by
  an independent agency.
